title: Coroner's inquest declares Arnaud's 2004 death a homicide
article: A coroner's jury has determined the death of a Vanderhoof man in 2004 was homicide by an RCMP officer in the line of duty.

The jury handed down its decision and recommendations Friday in the death of Kevin St. Arnaud on Dec. 19, 2004. St. Arnaud was shot three times by RCMP Const. Ryan Sherematta on the playing field of Nechako Valley Secondary school.

The five-person jury heard that St. Arnaud had been drinking the night before and, while happy at first, had then become depressed. His former common-law spouse testified to his state of intoxication.
There was also testimony from a man who got into a fight the night before with St. Arnaud at a bar.
Just before 1 a.m. that morning, the alarm went off at the Rexall Pharmacy at the Co-Op Mall. Sherematta and partner Const. Colleen Erickson responded to the call.
A man ran through the door of a restaurant in the mall and headed in the direction of the school.

Sherematta followed and, he testified, fired three shots after St. Arnaud started advancing on him in a threatening manner. He testified he fired after falling down, lying on his back, while Erickson testified the shots were fired while Sherematta was still on his feet, in a combat stance. A forensic pathologist also testified that the bullets had apparently been fired downwards, not upwards.
Sherematta testified he was afraid St. Arnaud had a gun. A search of the body revealed no weapon.
The inquest lasted six days, and the jury made seven recommendations designed to avoid a repeat occurrence.

Several of those were addressed to the RCMP in Vanderhoof in Prince George and included changes to staffing levels on evenings, weekends and holidays, having officers properly identify themselves when involved in investigating incidents, and that personnel receive as much information as possible when responding to an alarm.

It also recommended the mall ensure potential access sites on the roof be secured. It is believed the robbery suspect gained entry to the pharmacy through the roof. The jury also recommended the B.C. Liquor Distribution Board review and ensure correct enforcement of sales of alcohol in licensed premises.
The inquest was called by then-Regional Coroner Shane DeMeyer after the Crown indicated last February that it would not be proceeding with charges.
